claims.text: A solution-treatment-plus-aging process will produce nanoscale, heterogeneously distributed secondary-phase precipitates in a high-entropy alloy.
The precipitate-containing microstructure will simultaneously improve strength, ductility, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance relative to conventionally processed HEAs.
The proposed initial material is a conventionally cast or homogenized HEA with a predominantly single-phase microstructure.
High-temperature solution treatment homogenizes the alloy.
Controlled aging precipitates nanoscale secondary phases in a heterogeneous distribution.
The proposed improvement requires an alloy composition capable of forming stable second phases during aging.
The thermal cycle must avoid excessive precipitate coarsening for the proposed improvement to occur.
Excessively coarse precipitates would lead to embrittlement.
Nanoscale heterogeneous precipitates pin dislocations.
Nanoscale heterogeneous precipitates refine the grain structure.
Nanoscale heterogeneous precipitates alter microscale load distribution.
The precipitates increase strength through precipitation strengthening.
The precipitates permit continued plastic deformation by obstructing without completely blocking dislocation motion, thereby improving ductility.
A refined multiphase microstructure can increase the effective Young’s modulus.
A refined multiphase microstructure can improve fracture resistance by toughening grain boundaries and distributing localized stresses.
The treatment is expected to increase strength by more than 10–15% relative to conventional processing.
The treatment is expected to increase fracture toughness relative to conventional processing.
The treatment is expected to maintain or slightly improve ductility relative to conventional processing.
The treatment is expected to increase effective Young’s modulus relative to conventional processing.
The hypothesis may fail when precipitate formation is kinetically limited or when precipitates coarsen adversely during aging.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis and falsification rule require improved ductility, whereas the predicted outcome allows ductility merely to be maintained. A result with unchanged ductility would therefore satisfy the predicted outcome but falsify the stated hypothesis under the stated rule.
